ANALYSIS REPORT
==============================================================
Topic:      Evaluate SQL versus NoSQL for a high-traffic e-commerce platform.
Prepared:   20 February 2026
Draft:      Initial
==============================================================

OVERVIEW
----------------------------------------
This report examines: Evaluate SQL versus NoSQL for a high-traffic e-commerce platform.

The analysis draws on 4 research angles, each focused on a different dimension of the problem. The goal is not a single verdict but a clear picture of the considerations that should inform a decision — because the right answer is always context-dependent.

FINDINGS
----------------------------------------

[1] Compare consistency guarantees and transaction support between relational and document stores.
    Every infrastructure component you self-host is one more operational responsibility. The build-vs-buy calculus compounds quickly in distributed systems.

[2] Analyse how query patterns and data access shapes should drive database selection.
    Documentation is the hidden cost of any distributed system. A well-documented monolith is faster to navigate for a new hire than an undocumented service mesh, regardless of code quality.

[3] Examine scaling stories in practice - where SQL struggles and where NoSQL introduces its own problems.
    Documentation is the hidden cost of any distributed system. A well-documented monolith is faster to navigate for a new hire than an undocumented service mesh, regardless of code quality.

[4] Review operational concerns: schema evolution, backup strategies, and migration complexity across both families.
    Service mesh infrastructure (Istio, Linkerd) solves cross-cutting concerns like mTLS and rate limiting but adds its own operational surface area that teams must learn to manage.

CONCLUSION
----------------------------------------
No single architecture, tool, or approach is universally correct. What the findings above show consistently is that the best choice is the one aligned with current constraints-not the one that looks best on a whiteboard.

Before committing, ask: do we have the team, tooling, and operational maturity to support this? If that answer is uncertain, the safer path is usually the simpler one, with a deliberate plan for when to evolve it.
reviewer_feedback: Well-structured report. The findings are specific, the conclusion is actionable, and each section earns its place.
